Adventure journal / Events, native Windows Steam + Classic 53.16

Source images are data/runtime/native-pe-images.json reference and classic.
Steam: PE:6a70a6d9:02711000
  SHA256 205770918fd54c96cbbcf89223ebd449e2e113c7c873ed81177c4511a3450db7
Classic: PE:6a70b91c:0270a000
  SHA256 f35bbaf37aa96f93f95f8a35a9341e6649da46bc29a8650316bfdc2dfc57f3e4

These are source reconstructions from the configured original PE images, not
runtime observations or translator simulations. pe-*-ghidra-decompiled.c and
individual pe-*-journal-*.c files are actual Ghidra 12.1.4 decompiler output.
The existing DecompileJournalAgreementsPE.java generic PE-manifest interface
was reused; its assigned agreement_ symbol prefix is a tool label, not a claim
that Events uses the Agreements title constructors. No inferred C replaces
the decompiler output. Inferred field names below are paired with actual RVAs.

pe-functions.tsv retains the original unwind extent, executable-code extent,
image identity, image path and digest. pe-ghidra-functions.tsv feeds exact
executable extents to Ghidra. MSVC's trailing embedded switch/remap bytes are
retained as pe-switches.tsv, not decoded as instructions. The ASM, branches,
conditions, calls and literal operands retain aliases, omitted-field exits,
packed stores and native fallbacks. There are 18 owners/leaves per edition:
renderer; card construction; incident/history titles; hearing/mission;
incident index; performance; calendar; caste/entity/site/building/region/
underground/artifact/religious-office suppliers; both native wrap functions.

Native producer correspondence (RVA, Steam / Classic)
  c2110 / c20a0  complete journal renderer
  d4f50 / d4ee0  event card construction and event occurrence date
  d53a0 / d5330  incident title
  d7080 / d7010  historical title
  d8440 / d83d0  hearing, common knowledge and mission paragraphs
  d9880 / d9810  incident index/search terms (not whole display titles)
  65f420 / 65ce40  performance title
  773390 / 770db0  calendar month leaf
  8e7310 / 8e4b80  single-string wrapper into vector wrapper
  8e7440 / 8e4cb0  complete paragraph vector -> native wrapped row vector

Complete title selector families
  Incident: 11 values, 0..10, dispatch d53f4 / d5384.
    0 death; 1 crime; 2 attack; 3 escalated attack; 4 reunion;
    5 demand of submission; 6 performance; 7 artifact action;
    8 written-work action; 9 self-identification; 10 refusal to identify.
    Unsupported values exit without a title. Participant ownership uses the
    native adventurer ID. Names and RAW caste words remain dynamic fields.
  Crime: 19 values, 0..18, dispatch d62c6 / d6256.
    production order violation; export prohibition violation; job order
    violation; conspiracy to slow labor; crime of murder; disorderly conduct;
    building destruction; vandalism; crime of theft; crime of robbery;
    crime of blood-drinking; embezzlement; crime of attempted murder;
    crime of kidnapping; crime of attempted kidnapping; crime of attempted
    theft; crime of treason; crime of espionage; bribery.
    Absent/unsupported crime retains the ownership prefix alone.
  Artifact: 6 actions, 0..5, dispatch d5859 / d57e9.
    possession of; placement of; gaining of; giving of OBJECT to RECIPIENT;
    refusal to give OBJECT to RECIPIENT; The destruction ofOBJECT.
    The native incident destruction string has no space after "of".
    Actions 0..4 keep location precedence: building-in-site / site, otherwise
    surface region, otherwise underground region. Empty formatted fields do
    not remove their independently appended possessives/connectives.
  Written work: 2 actions, 0/1: placement / giving; reuse recipient/location
    handling. Missing work record gives "an untitled work"; an existing work
    with an empty title can still contribute no bytes.
  Historical: 34 values, 0..33, dispatch d70d1 / d7061.
    0 march toward; 1 abduction; 2 incident-index initialization;
    3 occupation; 4 person presence; 5 entity presence; 6 harassment;
    7 flight; 8 abandonment; 9 reclamation; 10 foundation;
    11 march to reclaim; 12 march to found a site; 13 withdrawal;
    14 insurrection; 15 overthrow / failed insurrection / insurrection crushed;
    16 ascension to office; 17 claim; 18/19 accept/refuse offer of tribute;
    20/21 accept/refuse demand for tribute; 22/23 accept/refuse offer of peace;
    24 cessation of tribute; 25 presence in site and optional building;
    26/27 presence in site; 28 possession; 29 absence from site and optional
    building; 30/31 absence from site; 32 lack of possession; 33 destruction.
    Ghidra's inner default label for presence is the 26/27 alias, not support
    for arbitrary enum values: the original unsigned <=33 guard comes first.
    Outcome 0/1/2 branches retain independently optional entity/site IDs;
    unsupported outcome retains "The ". Office suffix distinguishes entity
    office and religious site. Fixed connectives can survive empty names.
  Performance: 8 values, 0..7, dispatch 65f4cb / 65ceeb.
    story/history; poem/poetic form/written work; music/form/composition;
    dance/form/work; sermon on person; sermon on sphere; sermon on value;
    sermon on worthlessness of value. Values 6/7 share a block and differ by
    signed value strength. The subordinate value switch has 33 values 0..32.
    Musical roles select playing/singing/chanting/speaking/performance; dance
    role 3 selects dancing. Native venue handling is independent of core
    topic validity, so a venue-only title is reachable. Existing memory-story,
    memory-poem, memory-performance-work and memory-sermon-topic grammars own
    the nested topic fields. Native names remain complete dynamic fields.

Paragraph families
  One occurrence-date production:
    This event occurred on the DAY+ORDINAL MONTH in the year SIGNED_YEAR.
  Six hearing productions (3 lead-ins x optional informant):
    You heard this on the DATE[ from INFORMANT].
    You last heard this on the DATE[ from INFORMANT].
    You first heard this on the DATE[ from INFORMANT].
  Five fixed paragraphs:
    This is common knowledge where you are from.
    You have been ordered to slay this creature.
    You have been ordered to drive these forces out.
    You have been ordered to clear the forces from this site.
    You have been ordered to cause trouble for these forces.
  Three location-state captions:
    Centered on first heard; Centered on last heard; Centered on location.
  Calendar: 12 month values 0..11 and four native ordinal endings st/nd/rd/th.
    Granite, Slate, Felsite, Hematite, Malachite, Galena, Limestone, Sandstone,
    Timber, Moonstone, Opal, Obsidian. Year values are signed decimal.
    An additional native default path (773393 unsigned cmp ecx,11; ja
    7734ae ret; Classic 770db3/770ece) appends NO month bytes. Occurrence
    always constructs its date; hearing only checks report/first/last IDs,
    not the validity/range of tick or year. Month is (tick/1200)/28 without
    modulo 12, and day is (tick/1200)%28 + 1. Thus tick 403200 reaches month
    12 and can visibly produce "This event occurred on the 1st  in the year
    250." or "You heard this on the 1st  in the year 250." with the same
    optional last/first and informant branches. The missing month leaves
    the two independently appended spaces. Negative tick division is signed
    and can also yield day zero/negative values; the out-of-range ordinal
    selector takes "th". These default/empty-date shapes have no extra text.

Hearing predicates in the original PE
  card+18 points to the native report. Compare report integers +2c/+30/+34/
  +38 with +48/+4c/+50/+54 to derive whether first and last records coincide.
  If report+2c != -1, emit the current/last paragraph: choose "You last" if
  the records differ and report+48 != -1, or if report flags at +28 have bit1;
  otherwise choose "You". Date uses year +30 and tick +34.
  If the records differ and report+48 != -1, emit "You first heard this" with
  year +4c and tick +50. Informant resolution is independently conditional;
  " from " is appended only after successful resolution to a nonempty name.
  The common-knowledge path also uses mask 2 at report+28 (bit1); report bit0
  supplies the separate card pin/display marker. All four mission paths remain
  distinct.
  Absent report/card payload branches append nothing; no text is fabricated.

Retained source, native blank separators and the cropped-card problem
  Event summary/card fields, byte offsets:
    +00 kind (0 incident, 1 historical)
    +68 complete title std::string (preserved)
    +a0 display fallback title std::string, shortened to 50 bytes
    +c0/+c8/+d0 vector<std::string*> of ALL native 50-column title rows
    +d8/+e0/+e8 vector<std::string*> of ALL native 58-column paragraph rows
  Occurrence text is wrapped at d5229 / d51b9. Current/last hearing text is
  wrapped at d90be / d904e; first hearing text at d9629 / d95b9. These calls
  receive the complete local paragraph as temporary source vector[0], append
  all rows to card+d8, then destroy the temporary. There is no persistent
  complete-body std::string field on the card.
  d8440 inserts a real zero-length string into card+d8 before each separate
  mission, hearing and common-knowledge paragraph. These native empty rows
  distinguish paragraph boundaries. They must not be merged across.
  The vector wrapper 8e7440 scans back to the word-break space, shrinks its
  outgoing row to INCLUDE that space, and skips only subsequent leading
  spaces. Concatenate retained row bytes within one native paragraph; do not
  insert a new space between rows or strip their original break spaces.
  This also preserves forced splits inside very long tokens.

  The normal compact renderer fixes card body height at 3 (c3077 / c3007).
  Expanded selected height derives from screen rows - upper margin - 6;
  unselected cards in that mode are skipped. Selected paragraph scrolling
  reads journal+25c. Other compact cards start at paragraph row 0.
  One/two title rows and single-line paragraph cases set the body starting
  row independently. The loop c3320..c3362 checks both the retained vector
  length and drawable bottom; when row > bottom it never calls addst for
  the hidden row. Thus the initial English row may lack the informant/end of
  date even though that text still exists in card+d8. A draw-only frame
  collector cannot reconstruct it by waiting for invisible addst calls.
  The comparison is strictly greater (c3325 cmp / c3328 jg): row == bottom
  is a real text row, even when that row carries the skin's lower border.
  A two-line title moves the first hearing row onto that inclusive edge.
  Stopping a consumer at y < border_bottom loses that entire hearing row;
  preserve the native inclusive text viewport rather than the skin interior.

  Display addst return sites are pe-display-fields.tsv:
    c3197 first title row; c31d9 next/full title; c3263 card counter;
    c335b native paragraph row; c34ff/c356d/c35d8 centered-state captions.
    Classic equivalents are c3127/c3169/c31f3/c32eb/c348f/c34fd/c3568.
  The actual card builder call c3072->d4f50 (Classic c3002->d4ee0) executes
  for each displayed card, including cards whose cached rows cause an early
  constructor return. src/native_journal_event_hooks.inc calls that original
  constructor first, retains complete +68 and ALL +c0 rows, and segments +d8
  using its real empty separators. Each retained source carries the vector
  owner, first row index, row text and native row-string addresses. Existing
  captures are reused only when these still agree. The display association
  uses native row addresses, so a visible first row can recover the complete
  already-retained paragraph even if its continuation is clipped by DF.

Dynamic suppliers and omitted values
  Missing entity/site/surface/underground/artifact records have explicit
  "an unknown civilization/site/region/underground region/artifact" fallbacks.
  Invalid race gives "creature" (and optional plural s). Existing language
  names and RAW words can be empty; appended connecting words remain native.
  Artifact unnamed-writing fallback is "Untitled"; other unnamed artifacts
  use the original complete item caption. Religious-office lookup appends
  " of " and the site's actual name only on the actual native success path.
  Underground unnamed type 0/1/2 supplies "the depths of the world", "the
  magma sea", or "the Underworld"; an unsupported existing type or the
  existing named-flag path can append no bytes. The outer title still keeps
  any already-appended " in ".
  Building formatter has 14 native type selectors, subtype 0/1/2 for dungeon/
  sewers/catacombs, an optional complete proper name and unknown-building
  fallback. Its fixed captions include counting house, hospital, guildhall,
  mead hall, keep, temple, library, tavern, dark tower, underworld spire,
  market, tomb, dungeon, sewers, catacombs and tower. Existing quest-building
  and journal-event-place/legends vocabulary own these dynamic fields.
  No text-constructor differences were found between these PE editions and
  the existing ELF title-family reconstruction. The PE source independently
  demonstrates why omitted existing names retain connectives and why the
  pre-existing six hearing templates need whole-paragraph recovery.

Reproduction uses the fixed Python to run tools/extract_adventure_journal_events_pe.py,
then Ghidra's analyzeHeadless.bat with -noanalysis -scriptPath tools
-postScript DecompileJournalAgreementsPE.java SOURCE_DIRECTORY EDITION.
EDITION is steam or classic and the imported file is that configured PE image.
Only the offline source manifests and decompiled source are written here.
This extraction does not claim that the final in-game appearance was observed.
